info.name: Aastrika Common Service
info.description:
All API endpoints for aastrika-common-service, grouped by controller: Certificate, Passbook, Leaderboard, Ratings.

Usage:
1. Import into Postman. The collection id is kept stable, so re-importing this file updates your existing collection in place (choose Replace if prompted) rather than creating a new one.
2. Set the collection variable `baseUrl` (default http://localhost:7011).
3. Requests carry test assertions on the expected HTTP status. In the Passbook folder, run 'Add entries' before the 'Duplicate add' error case.

request.description: Completion + certificate-generated status for (rootOrgId, programId, userId). 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND if no completion row exists (Postgres user_program_completion).
Resolves the downloadable certificate URL. 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND / 400 PROGRAM_NOT_COMPLETED / 404 CERTIFICATE_NOT_GENERATED depending on state.
Adds passbook entries for `userId` (from the body). The header user is stored as `createdBy`.
Reads the authenticated user's own passbook. The user comes from the `x-authenticated-userid` header.
Reads passbooks for a list of users. No auth header required; users come from the body.

item.name: Ratings
item.description:
The four implemented RatingsController endpoints. The meta-update and additional-tag ops jobs were removed as unused.

Notes:
- R1 (upsert) writes to Cassandra AND emits a Kafka event to dev.rating.event.
- R1/R3/R4/R5 share collection variables pointing at a verified-enrolled user+activity, so the aggregation actually completes. An unenrolled pair is silently dropped to the DLQ (see R10).
- R1 varies the rating each run: a zero delta is a no-op in the aggregation.

exec: // The aggregation is delta-based: it only touches ratings_summary when the rating
// actually CHANGES. Re-posting the same value is a silent no-op, so cycle 1..5 to
// guarantee a non-zero delta on every run.
// The rating row is written synchronously; the summary is updated by the Kafka
// consumer, so give it a moment before running R4.

body.raw:
{
  "activityId": "{{ratingActivityId}}",
  "activityType": "{{ratingActivityType}}",
  "userId": "{{ratingUserId}}",
  "rating": {{ratingValue}},
  "review": "This course was genuinely useful and clearly structured. The examples were easy to follow and the pacing felt right across every module.",
  "recommended": "yes"
}

request.description:
Create/update a rating. Emits a Kafka event unless it's a comment-only update.

Uses a verified-enrolled user: the aggregator drops events for users with no row in sunbird_courses.user_enrolments, so an unenrolled pair leaves the summary empty forever (see R10). The pre-request script varies the rating because a zero delta is a no-op.
Ratings for one activity across a list of users.

exec: // A missing summary row still returns 200 with response=null, which is easy to mistake
// for success. Assert it is populated so a dropped aggregation event fails loudly.
"null summary - the aggregation event was probably DLQ'd, check the consumer log"

request.description:
Star counts + latest reviews (enriched with reviewer first name).

Returns 200 with response=null when no ratings_summary row exists. Reviews only appear in latest50reviews when longer than 100 chars (REVIEW_MIN_LENGTH).

item.name: R10. Upsert by NON-enrolled user -> 200, but aggregation drops it

exec: pm.test("status is 200 (the upsert itself succeeds)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
// Deliberately NOT asserting on the summary: this request exists to show that a 200
// here does not mean the aggregation ran.

request.description:
Regression guard for the trap that this endpoint returns 200 either way.

The rating row IS written, but the consumer throws NotEnrolledException (RatingAggregationServiceImpl:57), which is non-retryable, so the event goes straight to rating.failedRating and ratings_summary/ratings_lookup are never touched. Nothing in the HTTP response hints at this - check the consumer log or the DLQ depth.

item.name: Assessment
item.description:
POST /v2/user/assessment/submit — the only consumed assessment endpoint. Scoring is in-memory (the answer key rides in the request: each option carries isCorrect + the user's userSelected/response). Returns the raw score summary with HTTP 201 (NOT the AppResponse envelope — preserved for the live client contract).

External calls: user validation (user-search) and content hierarchy (getParent/getContentType). For local testing point user.search-url at the mock (scripts/mock-content-service.py) and content.hierarchy-url at the real content service.

exec: pm.test("has score fields", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b).to.have.property("result"); pm.expect(b).to.have.property("correct"); pm.expect(b).to.have.property("total"); });

request.description: 1 correct + 1 incorrect + 1 blank -> result 33.33. Writes user_quiz_master + user_quiz_summary.
Writes user_assessment_master. The user_assessment_summary row is only written when the identifier's parent resolves to a Course (parentContentType == 'course').
userId 'invalid-user' -> the mock user-search returns count 0 -> 'Invalid UserId.' 400. (Against a real user service, use any non-existent userId.)
Body missing the required 'identifier' -> bean validation 400.
